summary: Maintain a semantic selection set, active item and focus independently while hierarchy rules prevent double-transforming parents and descendants.
objective: Additive, range, group and clear actions select predictable semantic objects through both spatial picking and a readable companion control.
applies_when: A user inspects, hides, compares or transforms more than one semantic scene object.
intent_signals: shift select a range in the scene tree
parent and child both move twice
example_prompts: Select several building modules from the scene or hierarchy and hide them together.
Transform a group without applying the delta twice to selected descendants.
negative_signals: transform selected parent and child independently
not_for: Single-object inspection with no set operation.
Region selection algorithms for dense point clouds.

principles: Store selection as semantic IDs. Keep the focused control, active item, range anchor and selected set as distinct state because each serves a different interaction role.
Declare hierarchy policy: selecting a group may select the group as one semantic object, its eligible descendants, or both for inspection, but a group transform must have a unique effective root set.
Spatial hits, tree rows, search results and Select All feed the same selection reducer so modifiers and clear behavior do not diverge by view.
Selection feedback must survive mesh or material replacement and remain distinct from scientific coloring, hover and locked state.
implementation: Map every hit or row to a stable semantic ID and expose a readable companion list or tree for essential selection tasks.
Define replace, toggle, add, range and clear actions explicitly. Do not infer platform modifiers inside the model reducer; input adapters translate them into those actions.

Before a group operation, reduce the selected set to effective roots by removing any selected descendant whose selected ancestor already carries that transform; compute and display the authored group pivot.
When objects become hidden, deleted, filtered or locked, apply a stated retention policy and announce the resulting selected count and active item through the companion UI.
Reset selection separately from resetting the scene model unless the product contract explicitly combines them.
observable_checks: Select a parent and child, apply one translation, and verify the child receives one world-space delta rather than two.
Run replace, additive, toggle, range, Select All and clear through spatial and companion paths; selected IDs, active ID and visible feedback agree.
Hide, delete, lock and recreate render nodes for selected semantic objects; the declared retention policy holds without stale highlights.
Keyboard focus can move without silently changing selection unless the chosen companion pattern explicitly uses selection-follows-focus.

creative_affordances: Use outlines, brackets, a temporary group hull or a shared pivot to show the selected set.
Offer named selection sets for assemblies, floors or analysis cohorts.
known_limits: The WAI listbox pattern applies to the companion DOM control, not directly to WebGL hit testing.
Hierarchy-selection semantics and modifier conventions are application contracts.
Authored and source-checked guidance; no assistive-technology or runtime test was run.

claims.statement: The WAI-ARIA APG listbox pattern describes two keyboard interaction models for multiple selection, recommends a model that does not require holding modifier keys while navigating, and distinguishes focus from selection except where selection-follows-focus is deliberately chosen.
claims.scope: Authoring-practice guidance for a companion DOM listbox; it does not define scene hierarchy semantics or certify canvas accessibility.

source_refs.locator: Keyboard Interaction: Multiple Selection; notes distinguishing focus and selection
